entry.title: What is a blocking high, and why does it bring heatwaves?

link.title: What is a blocking high, and why does it bring heatwaves?

entry.content:
In the mid-latitudes, weather usually moves from west to east, carried by the jet stream. Sometimes a large high-pressure system settles in the path of this flow and stays for days or weeks. Weather systems then have to go around it. This is an atmospheric block.

Under a block in summer, air sinks and warms as it descends, skies are clear and the sun heats the ground day after day. These are the conditions for a heatwave.

In my research I found that blocking are often already in place during record breaking heatwave begins, usually for a day or two before. Heatwaves that spend more of their life under a block tend to be more intense, but the block alone does not decide how long they last.
